notes: Shows political and public pressure over river recreation where NRW's monitoring is not designed for bathing risk, the gap that inland bathing water designation campaigns target.
summary: On 2 September 2026 the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability updated the Senedd on reports of illness linked to recreational use of the River Tawe, first raised in the Senedd on 2 June 2026. NRW had reviewed incident reports, water quality data and storm overflow information and found no evidence of pollution, permit non-compliance or another incident that would explain the illnesses or warrant enforcement. The statement noted that routine monitoring of the Tawe assesses Water Framework Directive condition rather than bathing water quality.
title: River Tawe illness reports: NRW review finds no pollution or permit breach to explain them; routine monitoring is not designed for bathing
